ptr.note: The caller's AVBufferRef * slot (never NULL). *pbuf NULL: av_realloc(NULL, size) + av_buffer_create, flagged REALLOCATABLE, written to the slot and owned by the caller (bytes uninitialised). *pbuf live: an equal size is a no-op; a sole, writable, REALLOCATABLE reference whose window starts at its buffer's data is av_realloc'ed in place (buffer and window data/size updated), even when it is a pool buffer: only av_buffer_realloc of an empty slot sets the flag, but pool_alloc_buffer keeps it on an allocator's result while taking over its opaque/free, so the in-place av_realloc frees or shrinks the block its BufferPoolEntry still records (recycled later: use after free; freed again at flush: double free); otherwise a new reallocatable buffer gets min(size, old) window bytes and replaces the reference in place via buffer_replace (slot pointer unchanged, old count dropped). Bytes past the old window are uninitialised. ENOMEM leaves *pbuf untouched. Rust: BufferReference::alloc_resizable (NULL slot), BufferReferenceMut::resize (fills the new tail), UninitBuffer::resize. A NULL window (size 0, from av_buffer_create(NULL, 0)) reaching the copy path makes C call memcpy(dst, NULL, 0), UB (UBSan nonnull-attribute, buffer.c:176/218); the Rust wrappers take that one case without C's memcpy. They run C's copy path themselves (alloc_resizable + copy + swap into the same struct, BufferReferenceMut::realloc_by_copy) for a NULL window and for any buffer with an opaque (pool buffers: the opaque is their entry; reallocatable buffers C made have none), so a pool buffer is never resized in place.
